title: Runtime sync and batching heuristics — synthesis (2026-07-12)
content:
Summary:
This note captures the runtime sync on 2026-07-12 where we reviewed recent kernel selection flips, KV cache warmup behavior, and batching heuristic changes from sprint-29. The goal is to synthesize observations, surface regressions, and list next steps for a tidy canary next week. This doc is intentionally concise; more microbench logs are linked above.

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marco, Ling, Samir, Rhea, offline: Daniel (gave perf traces)

High-level observations: 
- Kernel selection: the new selective-fallback patch (PR #2418) reduces p99 latency for transformer_xl variants on RTX-A5000 by ~12ms in our microbench (seq_len=512, batch=4). Good for tail, neutral for median. Need to validate on p4d.
- KV cache warmup: persistent cold-starts observed for long-chat workloads (prefix reuse < 15%). Warmup curve shows effective hit-rate only after ~120 tokens for small-ctx models. Prefetch probe reduced misses by ~7% but increased 95th by ~5ms in some configs.
- Batching heuristics: adaptive batching with dynamic_batch_window=40ms results in fewer small batches but amplifies latency variance for low-qps lanes. Static 10-20ms window still better for interactive workloads.

Measured numbers (representative):
- baseline (old kernels): p50=32ms, p95=78ms, p99=210ms (seq=512, batch target 4)
- selective-fallback: p50=33ms, p95=70ms, p99=198ms
- prefetch-probe on (aggressive): hit_rate +7%, p95 +5ms for small-batch lanes
- adaptive-batcher window=40ms: mean throughput +12% but tail +9ms for qps<1

Notes / context:
- The kernel flip improves cache locality on KV reads for the grouped-attention path; however, we saw a small memcopy uptick in the profiling traces (Marco). Investigate whether memcpy can be fused with kernel stage.
- Prefetch improvements are promising for bursty workloads (dedicated), but for hosted interactive customers the extra jitter is concerning. Might gate aggressive prefetch behind plan-tier.

Action items (owner, due):
1) Marco: run the selective-fallback patch across p4d mini-canary (subset of production traffic) and collect full-traffic p95/p99 by 2026-07-16. Link artifacts in PR comment.
2) Ling: instrument cache warmup histogram per-model and add a daily report to Console (temp flag) to track effective hit-rate across customers. Due 2026-07-20.
3) Samir: prototype a hybrid batch window that decays for low qps (start at 20ms then to 8ms after 2s of idle). Microbench + canary by 2026-07-19.
4) Rhea: create a risk matrix for enabling aggressive prefetch on hosted plans; include rollback plan and customer-facing note. Due 2026-07-18.
5) Aisha: coordinate SRE for observability spike (tracing knobs) to capture memcpy hotspots during kernel run. Request on-call slot for 2026-07-15.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should aggressive prefetch be limited to Dedicated only? Pros: improves throughput and cost there. Cons: jitter for hosted. Need product input by next sync.
- What is our acceptable p99 regression threshold when switching kernels? SLOs currently allow +10ms at p99 for non-SLA tiers, but this isn't codified in rollout automation.

Risks spotted:
- Canary could surface regressions on GPU families we haven't fully profiled (A100 vs A5000 vs P4). We must avoid global rollout until p4d results in CI.
- Observed intermittent OOM on a 16GB worker during aggressive prefetch; likely due to double-buffering of KV prefetch queues.

Short-term experiment plan (this week):
- Enable selective-fallback on canary pool (PR #2418) but cap traffic to 5% routed via canary router. (Marco)
- Run comparative sweep of batch windows [8, 20, 40] ms on synthetic traces that mimic low-qps chat and high-batch embedding workloads. (Samir)
- Add a lightweight trace span around memcpy in kernel pipeline so we can correlate with GC and scheduling anomalies. (Aisha + SRE)

Longer-term items (backlog):
- Kernel fusion to eliminate separate memcopy (work item, depends on compiling new CUDA kernels).
- Per-customer batching policies surfaced in Console with cost/latency tradeoff slider.
- Cache pre-warming for managed long-chat sessions (session affinity + prefill).

Links and refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/2418
- JIRA: INF-987 (kernel selective fallback), INF-1009 (prefetch OOM report)
- Slack thread with traces: https://slack.com/archives/C01SERVE123/p1628872345000300

Tiny retrospective: this sync felt more aligned than last week — fewer action-item duplications and clearer owners. Keep the momentum on cross-team tracing so we can trust canary numbers.

Next sync: 2026-07-19, 10:30 PT — agenda: p4d results, canary metrics, decision on prefetch gating.

Appendix (quick checklist):
- [ ] Canary rollout cap configured (5%)
- [ ] Canary observability dashboard created
- [ ] Prefetch risk matrix draft
- [ ] Memcopy span added to tracer

End.
